expectations.text: The halved drinks budget is rejected: removing alcohol shifts what people drink, not how much they drink.
expectations.evidence: "Going dry changes what people drink. It does not reduce how much they drink."

expectations.text: Total drink volume is planned at roughly last year's overall level, redistributed to non-alcoholic lines.
expectations.evidence: "Treat roughly 2 non-alcoholic drinks per head as the starting scenario, not 0.6." Last year was about 2.1 per head.

expectations.text: Under-forecasting the soft-drink and energy-drink line while over-ordering coffee is called out as the specific modelling error.
expectations.evidence: "soft and energy drinks get under-forecast while coffee gets over-ordered."

expectations.text: The non-alcoholic order is specified at its own per-item granularity with its own quantities, not as a rounding-up of a generic order.
expectations.evidence: "Price the non-alcoholic line at the same per-item detail as last year's alcoholic one, with its own quantities."

expectations.text: The end-of-table water jug framing is rejected as insufficient provision.
expectations.evidence: "A jug and juice at the end of the snack table fails the provision test."

expectations.text: The dry posture is named where the evening is announced, not discovered on arrival.
